threads.body: This entry is placed under `### 🌟 New instrumentation`, but this PR adds configuration options to existing instrumentations rather than introducing new instrumentation modules (that section is reserved for entirely new modules such as SOFARPC/HBase). The analogous logback `capture-template` change was recorded under `### 📈 Enhancements` (see CHANGELOG.md:790-794). Consider moving this entry to an `### 📈 Enhancements` section for consistency.

replies.body:
Good catch on the duplication. Turns out that line isn't purely redundant though: for the `Logger.log(Level, Throwable, Supplier<String>)` overload, jboss-logmanager doesn't have its own advice for that particular JDK-declared method, so the call falls through to `java.util.logging.Logger`'s default implementation and ends up going through the java-util-logging instrumentation instead — without `java-util-logging.experimental-log-attributes=true` enabled, `thread.name`/`thread.id` are dropped for that path and `JbossLogmanagerTest` fails (verified locally).

Extracted the three shared `-D` flags into a `commonTestJvmArgs` list reused by both `test` and `testCaptureTemplateAndArguments` instead, so the flag stays in exactly one place without being copy-pasted. Pushed in 66b168f9.
Good idea, that's cleaner. Switched to `tasks.withType<Test>().configureEach { ... }` for the shared jvm args instead of the custom list. Pushed in 6cd6beec.

threads.body: The `satisfies(EXCEPTION_STACKTRACE, ...)` assertion becomes a no-op when `logException` is false, so the test would still pass even if a stacktrace attribute were unexpectedly present. It should explicitly assert that the stacktrace attribute is absent in the non-exception case (e.g., `val.isNull()`).
